cases.title: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation
cases.posture: Appeal against refusal of regular bail in an economic-offence prosecution

chunks.evidence: The object of bail is to secure the appearance of the accused person at his trial by reasonable amount of bail.
chunks.context: The Court distinguished securing attendance at trial from using pre-trial custody as punishment.
chunks.indexText: regular bail personal liberty economic offence accused appearance at trial detention is not punishment flight risk witness tampering Article 21 bail is the rule

chunks.evidence: The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventative. Deprivation of liberty must be considered a punishment.
chunks.context: The judgment discusses proportionality, presumed innocence, trial attendance and unsupported allegations of witness tampering.
chunks.indexText: pretrial custody not punitive presumed innocence prolonged trial documentary economic case regular bail no material supporting witness tampering

cases.title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation
cases.posture: Supreme Court directions and guidelines concerning arrest, bail and unnecessary pre-trial detention

chunks.evidence: The principle that bail is the rule and jail is the exception has been well recognised through the repetitive pronouncements of this Court.
chunks.context: The Court connects bail jurisprudence with Article 21 and the presumption of innocence.
chunks.indexText: regular bail jail exception Article 21 personal liberty presumption innocence appearance trial unnecessary arrest prolonged custody

chunks.evidence: Detention in custody pending completion of trial could be a cause of great hardship.
chunks.context: The judgment reiterates that pre-trial detention should not operate as punishment and issues category-based bail guidance.
chunks.indexText: trial delay long custody detention hardship bail guidelines investigation arrest charge sheet conditional release

cases.title: Bikramjit Singh v. State of Punjab
cases.posture: Appeal concerning default bail under Section 167(2) CrPC and the UAPA/NIA special-court framework

chunks.evidence: Once the maximum period for investigation of an offence is over, the accused shall be released on bail.
chunks.context: The Court examined when the indefeasible right to default bail arises under Section 167(2).
chunks.indexText: default bail statutory bail section 167 charge sheet deadline investigation period indefeasible right UAPA NIA personal liberty

chunks.evidence: The right to default bail is part of the procedure established by law under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
chunks.context: The Court treated default bail as a fundamental protection and set aside the refusal of relief.
chunks.indexText: fundamental right Article 21 default bail statutory period charge sheet filed application before challan personal liberty

cases.title: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)
cases.posture: Constitution Bench reference on the duration and conditions of anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC

chunks.evidence: The normal rule should be not to limit the operation of the order in relation to a period of time.
chunks.context: The Court held that anticipatory-bail protection need not invariably end at a fixed stage, while permitting case-specific conditions.
chunks.indexText: anticipatory bail pre-arrest bail section 438 duration time limit charge sheet trial conditions personal liberty

chunks.evidence: The protection granted under Section 438 should not invariably be limited to a fixed period.
chunks.context: The Constitution Bench answered the reference on duration and emphasized fact-specific judicial conditions.
chunks.indexText: pre arrest protection anticipatory bail continues trial court summons charges framed fixed period witness intimidation absconding conditions

cases.title: P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement
cases.posture: Appeal against refusal of anticipatory bail during a PMLA investigation

chunks.evidence: Grant of anticipatory bail at the stage of investigation may frustrate the investigating agency in collecting useful information.
chunks.context: The Court considered the nature of the money-laundering allegations, investigation stage and claimed need for custodial interrogation.
chunks.indexText: anticipatory bail refused PMLA money laundering economic offence custodial interrogation ongoing investigation gravity flight risk section 438

chunks.evidence: In the result, the appeal is dismissed. It is for the appellant to work out his remedy in accordance with law.
chunks.context: This is a contrasting precedent concerning anticipatory bail in a serious economic-offence investigation.
